precepts.text: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream. My servant Moses is not so: with him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. The only one the Lord spoke with mouth to mouth was Moses. When you hear black women go, God told me: God tell you nothing. Stop lying. The Lord spoke to me this morning, his voice was so clear: that's a lie. But people be believing this crap. Miriam said God spoke to me too, and she was a prophet; wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
precepts.point: They are prophets of the deceit of their own heart.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.” He did not send these pastors, these Christian reverends. Yet they ran: I am going to build a church here. I have not spoken to them: when they say God spoke to me, it is a lie. And “I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.”

How did the Lord speak to his prophets? “Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.” “My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.” “With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold”.

The only one the Lord spoke with mouth to mouth was Moses. So when you hear black women go, God told me: God told you nothing. Stop lying. The Lord spoke to me this morning, his voice was so clear: that is a lie. But people believe this crap.

Miriam said God spoke to her too, and she was a prophet, and the Lord answered, “wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?” If even a true prophet was rebuked for putting herself beside Moses, what about these pastors who say God spoke to them? They should have stood in his counsel and caused the people to hear his words; that is the only way to turn the people from their evil way, and you can only transform them with the Bible, the commandments of God.

precepts.point: Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew's child by his circumcision, not his colour. Reuel's daughters called Moses an Egyptian.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
When Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children”. How did she know? He was circumcised. You never read about Moses getting circumcised; he was already cut, because some of our forefathers retained that custom from our fathers. Outside of that, she would not have known the difference, because Egyptians and Hebrews were both black.

Then Moses fled to Midian and helped the seven daughters of the priest of Midian at the well, and they told their father Reuel, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took Joseph for an Egyptian. Reuel, Jethro, gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

Numbers 12:1 shows what that family was: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman”. She was Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, a priest of Midian but not a Midianite. Ethiopians are children of Ham, Kushites, the family of the Egyptians. A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one, and they still took Moses for an Egyptian. If he had been a white man, they would have known he was no Egyptian.

Paul passed for one too: “Art not thou that Egyptian”, the chief captain asked, and Paul answered, “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Moses passed for an Egyptian, Joseph passed for an Egyptian, Paul passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That's the point.

precepts.text: With Moses the Lord spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches, and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold; Moses saw the back parts, not the face.
precepts.point: Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by; and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts, but my face shall not be seen. Moses beheld the similitude of the LORD, the back parts of his glory, never his face.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”

The similitude of the Lord is what Moses beheld: the back parts of his glory, never his face. “Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.” In verse 11 Christ spoke to Moses on the Lord's behalf, with Moses as the mediator to the people; here it is the Father of heaven and earth himself, who put Moses in a clift of the rock and covered him with his hand while his glory passed by. “And I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.” That is speaking mouth to mouth, even apparently, and still no man sees his face and lives.

precepts.text: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman, and the Lord heard it.
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again. That is the same law working here: the leper is put without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 13: The Law of the Plague of Leprosy

precepts.why:
Miriam is the example of the leper put without the camp. “Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married.” They said, “Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?”

Miriam was trying to usurp authority over the man. “And the Lord heard it.” What followed shows the law of Leviticus 13 in motion.

precepts.text: The cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow.
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again. That is the same law working here: the leper is put without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 13: The Law of the Plague of Leprosy

precepts.why:
The Lord heard Miriam speak against Moses, and the judgment came: “the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.”

Here is a leper “in whom the plague is”, the very case Leviticus 13:45-46 speaks of, and it came upon her for speaking against Moses.

precepts.text: Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that received in again; the leper dwells without the camp.
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again. That is the same law working here: the leper is put without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 13: The Law of the Plague of Leprosy

precepts.why:
“the leper in whom the plague is” is defiled all the days the plague is in him: “he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his habitation be.” That is exactly what happened to Miriam.

“And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again. And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.”

That is the same law working here: the leper is put without the camp, and only when she was clean was she received in again.

precepts.text: The priest of Midian had seven daughters who came to water their father's flock.
precepts.point: They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses “because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married.” Who is she? Go back to Midian. “Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.”

This is where Moses came in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt: to the priest of Midian and his daughters. The Ethiopian woman is one of these daughters, the wife the Lord allowed him to marry. A place being called Midian and the woman called an Ethiopian is no contradiction.

precepts.text: Moses was content to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter; this is the same woman called the Ethiopian.
precepts.point: They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
“And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.” The Ethiopian woman of Numbers 12 is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, and whom the Lord allowed him to marry.

Miriam and Aaron did not speak against Moses over her when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women. The murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it: “Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.”

precepts.text: They that despise government, presumptuous and selfwilled, are not afraid to speak evil of dignities, the same spirit that speaks against the men the Most High sets up.
precepts.point: He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
The Lord Himself declared the difference between Moses and a prophet: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, “who is faithful in all mine house”, He speaks “mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches.” Then He asked, “wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”

Peter names that spirit: “them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Miriam and Aaron were not afraid to speak against the man the Most High set up; that is despising government, presumptuous and selfwilled.

It is the same spirit today that speaks against the men the Most High sets up, and Moses was very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth, when they did it.

precepts.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord; and fathers, provoke not your children to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
precepts.point: This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household.

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
When Moses cried, “Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee”, the Lord answered, “If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days?” The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place. Had Miriam been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord.

“And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.” Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household, as Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days and the people journeyed not till she was brought in again.

precepts.text: With Moses the Most High spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; that is why Israel saw no similitude and heard plain commandments.
precepts.point: Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream. My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house. With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches”.

That is why Israel “saw no manner of similitude on the day that the Lord spake unto you in Horeb”. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches. When the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant: fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill. It was simple and easy to understand.

So Israel is charged to take good heed, “Lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female”. Plain commandments leave no room for the graven images of Egypt.

precepts.text: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married.
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.” Here is what happened by the way: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.”

Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. That speaking is what brought on her what the Lord did unto her.

precepts.text: The anger of the Lord was kindled, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow.
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
What the Lord did unto Miriam: “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against them; and he departed. And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.”

For speaking against Moses, the anger of the Lord was kindled, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. That is what Israel is told to remember by the way.

precepts.text: If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days?
precepts.point: The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again.”

Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue to speak against Moses. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding. Remember what the Lord did unto Miriam.

precepts.text: When Miriam spoke against Moses she was struck with leprosy, white as snow, and was shut out of the camp seven days.
precepts.point: Moses said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High. Miriam was a prophetess and one of the chief women, and she led the women; women have a real role in the nation, but leading the body is not it. When Miriam got puffed up and spoke against Moses, she was judged.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
When Miriam got puffed up and spoke against Moses, she was judged: “And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.”

She was struck with leprosy, white as snow, and was shut out of the camp seven days. Women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; Miriam led the women, and when she rose against the man the Lord set over the congregation, the Lord judged her for it.

precepts.text: The Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud and stood in the door of the tabernacle; he came down in a cloud to speak, just as David describes.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“And the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam”. He came down in a cloud to speak, just as David describes.

David sang, “He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under his feet. And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind. And he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies.” That is how the Most High travels, shielded in the darkness of the cloud, the same way he came down and spoke to Moses face to face.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
“(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)” Moses was the meekest man in all Israel. He submitted to God's will 100%. Here the term humble is often translated as meek, highlighting Moses' exemplary character in leading the Israelites with patience and reliance on God.

That is what meek means in Isaiah 61: humility, gentleness, and submission to God's will. Not soft. Meekness is strength under control, God's control. We all must be meek.
